idiom_name: enum state + coordinator actor + persisted row (SwiftData/Core Data) + Task deadlines
implementation_notes: Swift has no workflow runtime, so the idiomatic shape is an actor per process instance that owns an enum state and drives async steps: the actor serialises replies for one instance without locks, which is exactly the correlation guarantee a process manager needs, while persistence goes through SwiftData/Core Data (or a server-side store the app talks to) after every transition. Deadlines come from racing a reply task against Task.sleep/ContinuousClock in a task group, or from a stored due date that is re-armed on launch. Durable coordination and idempotence remain application code; for short flows that never outlive the process, a plain async function with no persisted state is the simpler and correct choice.
pitfalls: Task.sleep is not a durable timer: after a process restart the deadline is gone, so due dates must be persisted and re-armed at launch or by a background task.
Actor reentrancy: any await inside handle lets the next reply interleave, so mutate the state before the first suspension point or split the handler into decide and perform phases.
Unstructured Tasks detach from the instance lifetime; without cancelling them on teardown a restarted coordinator can run old work twice.
Persisting to SwiftData on the main actor from a background coordinator can deadlock or block; use the appropriate ModelActor/background context for writes.
